name: Fat tames tannin
line: Tannin grips your tongue; fat and protein give it something softer to grab, so a firm red tastes smoother next to aged cheese or salami.

name: Acid cuts richness
line: Bright acid in wine, fruit or pickles rinses butterfat off your palate, so the next bite of a creamy cheese tastes as good as the first.

name: Salt loves sweet
line: Salt makes sweetness taste rounder and sweetness makes salt taste less harsh, which is why ham and melon or blue cheese and honey work.

name: Match the weight
line: Light with light, bold with bold. A delicate cheese disappears next to a heavy red; a pungent one flattens a crisp white.

name: What grows together goes together
line: Foods and drinks from the same region grew up on the same tables, so Manchego and Rioja or Parmigiano and Lambrusco rarely miss.

name: Contrast the texture
line: Crisp against creamy and chewy against crunchy keeps every bite interesting; bubbles do the same job in a glass.
